turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Come on through. Doctor's just wrestling with the computer, so grab a seat.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yep, sorry, this screen's having a moment. Right. What's brought you in?
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): The hernia wound. It's gone red and it's leaking, and I felt shocking last night. Been waiting since half past nine, so I'm not exactly cheerful.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): The repair was recent? When did they do it?
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): Ten days ago. Open repair, right groin, at the base hospital. Car park was a shocker, but that's beside the point.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sorry, ten days? Say it again, I clicked the wrong letter.
[SEG0007] person_3 (PATIENT): Ten days. Not a fortnight, ten days.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): What's coming out of it?
[SEG0009] person_3 (PATIENT): Um, yellow. Sticky. Not pouring out, but the pad's wet by lunchtime, and it smells a bit... off.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Have you had a fever?
[SEG0011] person_3 (PATIENT): That dressing they used on the ward rips half my leg hair off. I told them and they still stuck it on.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll come back to the dressing. The fever — did you actually feel hot?
[SEG0013] person_3 (PATIENT): Last night, yeah. Shivering under the doona. Well, actually my wife reckoned I was burning up. Thermometer's gone missing, so no number from home.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): And this morning?
[SEG0015] person_3 (PATIENT): Not shivering now. Still washed out. The wound's what hurts.
[SEG0016] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): I'll take the dressing down. Tell me if it pulls.
[SEG0017] person_3 (PATIENT): Just get it off. I'm past being delicate.
[SEG0018] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Dressing's off. Lower end's red, about a fifty-cent piece round the stitches, yellow stuff on the gauze, skin's warm. It's not gaping.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): Say that once more? I was still in the discharge summary.
[SEG0020] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Red around the bottom stitches, fifty-cent size, yellow discharge on the gauze, warm to touch, edges together.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): Where's the pain, and how bad?
[SEG0022] person_3 (PATIENT): Right in the wound. Throbs if I walk, worse if I cough. It was settling, then — two days ago, yeah — it fired up again.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): Out of ten?
[SEG0024] person_3 (PATIENT): Six sitting. Seven when I cough. And I'm tired, properly tired, not just sick of the waiting room.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): Nausea or vomiting?
[SEG0026] person_3 (PATIENT): No vomiting. Appetite's a bit off. I managed toast.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any sense the hernia's popped back? A new lump?
[SEG0028] person_3 (PATIENT): No. It's flat. It's the cut, not the hernia.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Bowels and waterworks alright?
[SEG0030] person_3 (PATIENT): Both normal. Can we skip the full quiz, my head's starting to thud from all the questions.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): Is the headache real, or are you just fed up?
[SEG0032] person_3 (PATIENT): Fed up. No headache. Sorry. I'm snappy today.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): Which antibiotic did they send you home with?
[SEG0034] person_3 (PATIENT): Keflex. Capsules, from the chemist.
[SEG0035] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Discharge letter on the screen says cephalexin 500 milligrams, four times a day.
[SEG0036] person_3 (PATIENT): Nah. The box was 250. I took 250s, four times a day, same as the chemist wrote on it.
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sorry, 250 or 500? I've got both sitting here now. Which did you swallow?
[SEG0038] person_3 (PATIENT): 250 milligram capsules. If that letter says 500, somebody else mucked it up.
[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): How many days did you take it?
[SEG0040] person_3 (PATIENT): Five days... or was it seven? Four times a day, and I finished the pack. Which length they wrote has gone out of my head.
[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): Still taking it?
[SEG0042] person_3 (PATIENT): No. Stopped a couple of days ago. Saturday, or maybe Sunday. I wouldn't swear to the day.
[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): And for pain?
[SEG0044] person_3 (PATIENT): Panadol. Two of the 500 milligram tablets, so a gram, four times a day. That I've kept up.
[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any allergies to medicines?
[SEG0046] person_3 (PATIENT): No. Nothing.
[SEG0047] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Quick obs. Temperature 37.9, heart rate 96, blood pressure 132 over 84, oxygen sats 98 percent on air.
[SEG0048] person_2 (DOCTOR): Having a look now. Tender down the bottom, red, a small bead of pus if I press. Edges are together. No pocket of fluid underneath that I can feel.
[SEG0049] person_3 (PATIENT): Infected, then. I shifted a bag of soil in the shed yesterday. Knew I shouldn't.

[SEG0050] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'd call it a likely superficial wound infection. A stitch reaction is still possible, and the swab will help, but pus plus feeling feverish overnight leans me toward infection.
[SEG0051] person_3 (PATIENT): So what are we doing? I need a lie-down after this, not a lecture.
[SEG0052] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll get a wound swab sent for culture, and change the antibiotic to flucloxacillin.
[SEG0053] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Swab kit's here. Want me to take it now?
[SEG0054] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes. Swab the discharge for microscopy and culture.
[SEG0055] person_3 (PATIENT): Spell the new tablet out. Dose, times, days. Don't do the five-or-seven thing.
[SEG0056] person_2 (DOCTOR): Flucloxacillin 500 milligrams four times a day, by mouth, for seven days. Empty stomach, about an hour before you eat.
[SEG0057] person_3 (PATIENT): Those wreck my guts. Last time I had a penicillin-type one I lived in the bathroom.
[SEG0058] person_2 (DOCTOR): Start it today all the same. If the diarrhoea is nasty, ring us before you stop it. Clean dry dressing, change it daily, and leave the soil bags alone.
[SEG0059] person_2 (DOCTOR): And come back and see me in three days. Don't wait if the redness spreads, the fever won't settle, or the wound splits open.
[SEG0060] person_3 (PATIENT): Three days, and sooner if I'm worse. Are we done? I need that lie-down.
[SEG0061] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Swab's done and labelled. Reception'll book the three days and print the script on your way out.

procedures_and_investigations.name: wound swab for microscopy and culture

clinical_actions.description: Wound swab for microscopy and culture
Start flucloxacillin 500 mg four times a day by mouth for 7 days
Take flucloxacillin on an empty stomach, about an hour before food
If diarrhoea is nasty, phone the clinic before stopping the antibiotic
Keep a clean dry dressing on the wound and change it daily
Leave the soil bags alone
Do not wait if redness spreads, fever will not settle, or the wound splits open
Follow-up consultation
Reception to print the prescription and book the review
